chunks: And from him, from Fadalah, from Rifah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage,' so he said: 'The guardian who takes part [of the options] and leaves part, and it is not permissible for him to leave all of it.'

key_terms.عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ: The knot of marriage, referring to the marriage contract or the authority to conclude it
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ بَعْضًا وَيَتْرُكُ بَعْضًا: Takes part and leaves part, referring to selecting some candidates while excluding others

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'one in whose hand is the knot of marriage' and what are his powers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the scope of the *wali*'s authority during the marriage contract, specifically addressing the balance between the guardian's discretion and the woman's agency. The phrase 'taking some and leaving some' indicates that while the *wali* may have a say in selecting a suitor or approving a match, he cannot unilaterally reject all candidates, thereby preventing arbitrary exclusion and ensuring the marriage process remains open and just. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the *wali*'s role is supportive rather than absolute, preserving the validity of the woman's choice within the framework of guardianship.
